attributes.residual: TWO MECHANISMS, BOTH NAMED FROM THE ALIGNED VIEW, NEITHER CLOSED. (1) BLIT-LOOP ADDRESS WEB, +0x2c..+0x4c. The target keeps ONE callee-saved register for both roles in sequence: `add r28,r31,r27` (base+off), then the three argument loads at big displacements off it -- `lwz r3,7660(r28)`, `lwz r4,7644(r28)`, `lwz r5,7648(r28)` -- and only THEN `addi r28,r28,7640` to form the CTLBLIT pointer that must survive the call, reusing the same register because base+off is dead at that point. Ours forms the CTLBLIT pointer FIRST (`addi r29,r3,7640` at +0x34) and so keeps two live registers, r3 for base+off and callee-saved r29 for the blit, which costs the extra `addi` and turns the two argument loads into small-displacement b-relative forms (`4(r29)`, `8(r29)`). The residual is therefore the POSITION of one `addi` relative to three loads, and probe 1 shows the source spelling of that pointer does not reach it -- MWCC builds the same IR either way. (2) RGB OR-CHAIN SEED, +0x110..+0x140. The target seeds the packed colour with G<<8 (`rlwinm r0,r0,8,16,23` on the 232 field), then inserts R<<16 (`rlwimi r0,r6,16,8,15`), then B (`rlwimi r6,r3,0,24,31`), evaluation order G,R,B. Ours seeds with R<<16 and goes R,B,G. Both alternative source orders were measured and both are WORSE than the order already in the tree, which is the substantive result: the retained `B | R<<16 | G<<8` spelling is the best of the three, so the seed choice is not being driven by source term order at all. NEXT LANE: do NOT re-probe either the pointer spelling or the OR-chain term order -- three forms are recorded above. The untried axes are the third cluster at +0x78 (target `li` where we emit `addi`, flagged SHIFTABLE so its real home is elsewhere) and the `L[2] - h/2` argument computation at +0x134..+0x150, where the target emits `subf r4,r7,r4` early and a late `mr r6,r0` while we emit an `addi r6,r3,0` early and defer the `subf` past the argument set-up -- that one is an argument-evaluation-order question and has never been probed.
